description: Funding Rate Arbitrage — Crypto Perpetual Futures. A structurally different research program from Directions A/B/C: this tests whether a market-structure mechanism (the perpetual funding rate, which caps long/short imbalance) produces collectible, cost-positive carry historically. It is NOT a directional price-prediction test and does not use the DK-test/label-shuffle/DSR machinery built for Directions A-C. Validation is: fetch real historical funding rates, compute realized annualized funding yield, net against realistic Binance spot+perp trading costs, and check whether the result is durably positive across the sample window and multiple assets — not whether any single number exceeds a threshold once.
current_verdict_2026-07-28: NOT CURRENTLY DEPLOYABLE. Trial #4001's weak feasibility threshold (PASS) is SUPERSEDED by #4003's rigor pass: the mechanism is real (statistically significant, positive in the long run) but the CURRENT market regime's funding yield does not beat the T-bill risk-free rate after realistic costs, on either exchange tested. Do not deploy real capital to this strategy based on #4001's headline number alone.
stopping_rule_doc: N/A — different mechanism class, no DK-test stopping rule applies. Stop if realized net APY is not durably positive (>0 after realistic costs) across at least 2 independent assets and a >=180-day historical window.
sacred_holdout_path: N/A — this is a measurement of a market-structure fact (funding rate history), not an in-sample-fit-then-holdout-confirm test. No holdout is needed because there is no fitted model to overfit; the only question is whether historical funding cashflows, net of realistic cost, are/were positive.
notes: Registered 2026-07-28, per user direction: 'ผมจะเริ่ม funding rate arbitrage บน Binance/crypto ควบคู่ไปเลยตั้งแต่วันนี้ ไม่ต้องรอผล Trial #2001' — motivated by the reasoning that of the 4 canonical edge sources (risk premia, microstructure, behavioral, informational), this project has tested 'behavioral/technical' ~1050 times with no edge, but has not seriously tested 'risk premia' via crypto funding rate (Path B's carry trials 2001-2008 tested FX/XAUUSD interest-rate carry, a different mechanism).
Pre-registered BEFORE running scripts/funding_rate_arb_pilot.py, per the pre-registration discipline established this session (F27's lesson: never run-then-register).

This is a measurement/feasibility pilot, not a live trading system. No API keys, no order execution, no capital at risk. Public market-data endpoints only (ccxt, no auth required for funding rate history).

hypotheses.name: Perpetual Funding Rate Arbitrage — Historical Carry Feasibility
hypotheses.status: PASS_FEASIBILITY (not a live-readiness pass -- see caveats)
caveats_not_yet_modeled: This is unleveraged yield (2-3%/yr) -- modest, comparable to a savings account, not a large edge on its own. Standard crypto cash-and-carry uses modest leverage (commonly 2-3x) to scale this, which was NOT modeled here.

No margin/liquidation risk modeling -- the short-perp leg requires margin collateral and is subject to liquidation risk during sharp adverse price moves, even though the position is nominally delta-neutral (basis risk, funding-rate volatility, and exchange/counterparty risk are all real and unmeasured here).

No funding-rate volatility/regime-risk analysis -- 24-28% of periods were funding-negative; a real position pays during those periods, this pilot only checked the net over the full window, not worst-case drawdown or consecutive-negative-period risk.

Real trading (not a public-data pilot) requires actual API keys, capital, and exchange account -- explicitly out of scope for this measurement pilot per user instruction ('paper-test / small capital' is the next step, not yet started).
Single exchange (Binance) only -- no cross-exchange basis or funding-rate arbitrage considered.
hypotheses.instrument: BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT perpetual futures (Binance) vs. spot
hypotheses.hypothesis: Binance perpetual funding rate (paid periodically between long/short sides to anchor perp price to spot/index) has historically been net-positive-for-the-short-side (i.e. collectible via long-spot + short-perp cash-and-carry) by an amount exceeding realistic round-trip trading costs (spot maker/taker fee + perp maker/taker fee + estimated spread), on a sustained, multi-month basis, for at least BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT.
hypotheses.mechanism: Structural: perpetual contracts use a periodic funding payment (every 8h on Binance) between long and short positions to keep perp price tethered to the underlying index. A structural, persistent long-side crowding (common in bull-biased retail perp markets) creates a persistent positive funding rate, which a delta-neutral cash-and-carry position (long spot, short equal-notional perp) can collect without taking directional price risk. This is NOT a claim about predicting price direction.

frozen_params.position_rebalance: none (static cash-and-carry, held for full window)

hypotheses.economic_rationale: Distinct from Path B's carry trials (2001-2008), which tested FX/XAUUSD interest-rate-differential carry, a completely different funding mechanism, data source, and asset class. Crypto perpetual funding is driven by retail speculative demand imbalance, not central-bank rate differentials.
data_dependencies: Binance funding rate history (ccxt, public endpoint, no auth)
hypotheses.validation_plan: fetch_real_funding_history -> compute_realized_annualized_funding_yield -> net_of_realistic_costs -> check durability across full window and both assets -> PASS/FAIL (not a DK-test/p-value framework; see description field for why).

hypotheses.name: Perpetual Funding Rate Arbitrage — Live Paper-Trading Phase
hypotheses.mechanism: Same as #4001. This trial is the forward-testing phase: real, live price + funding-rate data (ccxt, no auth), simulated notional positions ($1000/leg, PAPER -- zero real capital, zero real orders), tracking the ACTUAL funding cashflow received/paid over real elapsed time. Not a backtest -- state persists between runs so the track record accumulates going forward only (bug found and fixed same day: first run incorrectly back-filled 100 pre-existing historical funding events as if they were new; fixed to anchor the funding-lookback window to the position's actual open time).
hypotheses.validation_plan: Re-run scripts/paper_trade_funding_arb.py periodically (every 8h, matching Binance's funding interval) with no arguments to record real funding events since the last check. Accumulate for >=180 days before drawing any conclusion (per #4001's stopping-rule doc). No action needed between runs beyond re-invoking the script. Not yet automated/scheduled -- currently requires manual re-invocation.
caveats: Not yet scheduled to run automatically -- someone/something needs to re-invoke this periodically for the track record to actually accumulate. A cron/scheduled-task wiring was NOT set up this session.
Same caveats as #4001 apply (unleveraged, no margin/liquidation modeling, single exchange).

result_summary.verdict: FAIL_RIGOR for deployment today. The per-period rate IS statistically distinguishable from zero (NW-significant on every exchange/window tested) -- this is a real structural cashflow, not noise -- but the CURRENT, recent-window magnitude does not clear the T-bill hurdle after realistic costs, on either exchange tested. The strong long-run headline number reflects a past regime (2022), not current conditions.

hypotheses.instrument: BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT on Binance AND a second exchange (OKX)
hypotheses.mechanism: Same as #4001/#4002. This trial applies the SAME rigor standard already used to reject Direction A/B to the last surviving 'edge': (1) Newey-West HAC significance test on the per-period net rate (identical formula/kernel to edge_search_cross_sectional.py's run_dk_test, reused deliberately for consistency) -- is the mean distinguishable from zero given autocorrelation; (2) cost stress at 1.0x/1.2x/1.5x realistic round-trip fees; (3) a second exchange (OKX) to check whether the mechanism is Binance-specific; (4) yield during 4 historical crypto crash windows (COVID Mar 2020, LUNA May 2022, Celsius/3AC Jun 2022, FTX Nov 2022) if data reaches that far back; (5) direct comparison to an assumed ~4.5%/yr T-bill yield -- explicitly NOT rationalizing past a negative result if net yield fails to beat risk-free.

frozen_params.significance_test: Newey-West HAC t-test, Bartlett kernel, T^(1/3) lag truncation, p<0.05 two-sided

hypotheses.stopping_rule_this_trial: If net-of-cost annualized yield does not exceed the assumed T-bill yield, OR the Newey-West test is not significant at p<0.05, the mechanism does NOT constitute a deployable edge over simply holding T-bills, regardless of the raw sign of the mean funding rate. This is a valid, informative result if it happens -- not a reason to lower the bar.
